header.institution: COLLEGE OF NATURAL AND SOCIAL SCIENCES

exam_paper.instructions: Show all the necessary steps to answer the following questions.

parts.label: a)
parts.text: does it satisfy the criteria for an integral test? Justify your answer.

parts.label: b)
parts.text: if your answer in (a) is yes, use integral test to determine its convergence.

questions.text: Use the generalized ratio test to show that the radius of convergence of the power series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n(x-c)^n$ is given by $R = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left| \frac{a_n}{a_{n+1}} \right|$ where $a_n$ is the coefficient of the power series.

If $f(x)$ is a non zero function and differentiable infinitely many times, then show by induction that the $n^{th}$ derivative of the power series representation of $f(x)$ is equal with its corresponding taylor series representation.
Use application of power series and $\int_{0}^{\infty} t^n e^{-t} dt = n!$ for a positive integer $n$ to find the formula of $\int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-t} \sin(tx) dt$ for $|x| < 1$.

Find the fourier cosine expansion of $f(x) = \begin{cases} x(\pi - x) & \text{for } 0 < x < \pi \\ -x(\pi + x) & \text{for } -\pi < x < 0 \end{cases}$ with period $p = \frac{\pi}{2}$ and prove that $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^2} = \frac{\pi^2}{6}$.
